automation_level.description: How much of this boundary a machine is allowed to decide on its own.

exec_summary.description: One plain-language sentence for a non-technical reader. No product or service names.

business_value.description: Why a leadership team should fund this boundary.

owner.description: Delivery team accountable for building and running this boundary.

human_accountable.description: Named human role that answers for this boundary's decisions.

build_wave.description: Delivery wave. 1 is the walking skeleton; 4 is the learning loop.

stage_order.description: Position of a workflow-step within its loop. Stage 0 is the always-on platform band; 1-7 are the factory loop; 8-12 are the runtime loop.

loop.description: Workflow-step only. Which band this stage belongs to. The platform band is always on; the factory loop runs once per solution; the runtime loop runs on every invocation of a published agent; the learning band closes both.

deployable_unit.description: The unit this boundary ships in: one repository, one deploy target, one release cadence. Required for anything with a build_wave. Must name a deployable-unit specification.

module.description: The in-repo module this boundary lives in: one directory, one public port. Callers outside the directory import the port and nothing else. Required alongside deployable_unit, and must be declared by that unit.

repository.description: Deployable-unit only. The repository name the harness team clones.

forcing_function.description: Deployable-unit only. Which forcing function justifies a separate process and repository rather than a module in the host. Absence of all five means this should be a module.

modules.description: Deployable-unit only. The module directories this unit contains. Every member component must name one of these.

consumes.description: The other side of someone else's api_contract. Each entry names a provider and one of its declared operations; an entry that names an operation the provider does not publish fails generation. This is what makes a contract change in one repository visible in another.

per_action.description: How many times the consumer calls this operation per unit of work on its hot path. Zero means the call happens off the hot path. Required once the consumer declares a hot_path, because a latency budget cannot be checked without a call count.

external_events_consumed.description: Signals that originate outside this platform and therefore have no emitter in the map. Declaring one here is the only way to consume an unemitted event; events_consumed is checked against emitters and fails generation otherwise.

serves_stages.description: Additional stages this component participates in beyond its home workflow_id. Used where the runtime loop deliberately reuses factory machinery rather than duplicating it.

reference_elements.description: Workflow-step only. Canonical boxes drawn in the reference diagram for this stage. Every element must be claimed by at least one component or the map reports a coverage gap.

reference_map.description: Component only. Reference-diagram elements this component implements. Unknown values fail generation.

data_owned.description: Authoritative state objects. Exactly one component may own each object.

open_questions.description: Honest unknowns. These surface in the map as amber, not as silent gaps.

api_contract.description: The callable surface. Each entry names exactly one caller and one worker.

caller.description: Who initiates. Always a named component, channel, or human role.

worker.description: Who performs the work and owns the result.

frequency.description: How often this operation is called, relative to the platform's units of work. per-action is the hot path: once or more for every step a running agent takes.

retrofit.description: What changing this operation's shape costs once it is in production. refactor: callers change, no stored data moves. migration: stored data has to be rewritten or backfilled. rewrite: the change is not available without redesigning callers around a different model. Only migration and rewrite have to be decided at 0-to-1; refactor is deferrable and deciding it early is over-engineering.

p95_ms.description: The latency budget this operation commits to at p95, in milliseconds. A budget, not a measurement — it is what callers are entitled to design against.

hot_path.description: Declared by a component that sits on a per-action path — one that runs for every step a running agent takes. Naming the unit of work and the overhead budget is what lets the generator add up what this component's own consumes already commit it to spending.

unit_of_work.description: The single thing this component does once, against which per_action counts are stated.

budget_p95_ms.description: The p95 overhead this component commits to for one unit of work, excluding time spent inside external systems.

cost.description: MVP running cost. Ranges are monthly USD for one non-production environment at the stated volume driver.

shared.description: True when the same instance is shared with other components. Shared lines are counted once in the platform rollup.
